guidance.heading: Financial Guidance
section: “With strong year-to-date performance and continued momentum in customer bookings, we remain on track to deliver on our full year outlook of approximately 7% Organic Revenue Growth, (or 16% on a reported basis), more than 24% growth in Adjusted EBITDA, and approximately $200 million in operating cash flow,” said Matthijs Glastra, Chair and Chief Executive Officer. “Our strong backlog, new product contributions and leading positions in markets benefiting from favorable long-term secular trends provide a solid foundation for future growth and value creation. Looking ahead to 2027, we expect reported revenue growth of more than 15%.”

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects GAAP revenue to be in the range of $306 million to $312 million, reflecting reported revenue growth of more than 18%. The Company also expects Adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $76 million to $79 million and Adjusted Diluted EPS to be in the range of $0.91 to $0.96 per diluted share, or 0% to 5% growth. The Company’s guidance assumes no significant changes in foreign exchange rates.

For the full year 2026, the Company now expects GAAP revenue to be in the range of $1,135 million to $1,140 million, reflecting reported growth of approximately 16%. The company expects Adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $274 million to $277 million, and Adjusted Diluted EPS to be in the range of $3.66 to $3.71 per diluted share, or 11% to 13% growth. The Company’s guidance assumes no significant changes in foreign exchange rates.

desk.headline: Revenue up 23% to $305m, beat; full-year sales and EBITDA range narrowed, EPS range trimmed
results: Revenue rose 23% to $305m, ahead of the company's own $300-304m guide; organic growth was 9.9% and the Riverpoint Medical deal added about 13%.
Adjusted EPS rose 21% to $1.05, while GAAP EPS fell to $0.05 from $0.30 on deal costs, intangible amortisation and higher interest.
Adjusted EBITDA jumped 38% to $80.3m and the margin widened to 26.3% from 23.4%.
Medical Solutions revenue grew to $160m from $123m with Riverpoint; Automation Enabling Technologies grew to $145m from $125m with a 50.2% gross margin.
Paying for Riverpoint (about $1.2bn in cash) took net debt to $689m; operating cash flow was $39.3m.

guidance.summary: Novanta tightened its 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges around similar midpoints but trimmed its adjusted EPS range; it guided Q4 revenue to $306-312m and expects reported revenue growth of more than 15% in 2027.

points: Bookings rose 29% (18% without Riverpoint) with a book-to-bill of 1.08, and every business booked above 1.
Shipments on a programme at the Stockport site are paused while an issue found in customer testing is fixed; restart is expected in Q1 2027.
That pause costs about 2 points of margin, so Q4 adjusted gross margin is seen near 46% rather than 48%, normalising around Q2 2027.
Riverpoint added about $33m of revenue in Q3 and is expected to add about $35m in Q4.
For 2027 management pointed to at least 15% sales growth, at least 20% adjusted EBITDA growth and gross margin up at least 1 point.
call.source: Call coverage: GuruFocus via Investing.com, 10 Nov 2026; prior ranges from the Q2 2026 results release

watch: Timing of the Stockport restart and whether Q4 margins land near 46%.
Paying down debt taken on for Riverpoint, now 2.2x net leverage.
Whether the strong bookings convert into the >15% growth flagged for 2027.
